verdicts.matching_evidence: There is an internal inconsistency regarding the percentage of the model kept frozen during fine-tuning. In the Abstract, the authors claim the framework trains approximately 4.15M parameters while 'keeping over 88% of the model frozen.' However, training 4.15M parameters out of a ~641M parameter architecture (the ViT-H backbone plus adapters) means that approximately 99.35% of the model remains frozen. The authors themselves correctly report that they are 'keeping over 99% of SAM parameters frozen' in Section V (Conclusions). The '88%' figure in the abstract severely understates the method's parameter efficiency and should be corrected to 99% to match both the arithmetic and the conclusion.

verdicts.matching_evidence: The mathematical formulation of the Conv-LoRA layer in Equation 1 is incorrect and contradicts the architecture shown in Figure 2(c). Equation 1 writes the expert and gating term as $g_i(x) E_i(W_E) x$. This notation implies that the convolutional expert $E_i$ is applied directly to the down-projection weight matrix $W_E$, with the result then multiplied by $x$. In standard Conv-LoRA implementations, the input $x$ is first projected to a spatial feature map $W_E x$, which is then passed through the convolution experts.
